A1-02.en: Okay. I'm out, I'm out of the water. / Those were crocodiles, two of them, and they were not curious. / They were patient.

A1-03.en: Okay, that's a body. A big one. / Something ate half of it last night and left. / Left, or stepped away.

A1-04.en: Look at the size of that bite. / My whole hand fits in one tooth mark. / I'm standing in its kitchen.

A1-05.en: I picked today on purpose. / Twelve hours from now, the sky over there catches fire. / I'm just here to watch.

A1-06.en: Turtle shell, size of a dinner plate. / There's a dry hollow under that far bank. / Crocodiles right below it. So, no.

A1-07.en: Palm fibre, twisted twice, through the gaps in the rim. / If this knot fails today, / I'm drinking from the crocodile pool.

A1-08.en: Forest is a solid wall, I can't see two metres in. / But that's a path. / Something big made it.

A1-09.en: Round footprint, wider than my shoulders. / Water inside is still cloudy, so it's fresh. / Whatever made this is close.

A1-10.en: There. Three of them, horned, grazing. / They're the biggest things in this valley. / Big means safe, I hope.

A1-S1.en: Okay, they're massive, but they only eat plants. / They'll completely ignore a tiny thing like me. / Just watch.

A1-13.en: He stopped. He stopped six metres short. / That was a warning, not an attack. / Message received, big guy.

A1-14.en: So I can't walk in. Not yet. / I sit here at the edge, where they can see me. / I don't move. And I wait.

A2-01.en: An hour, sitting right here, watching. / Watching who they listen to. And it's not the big guy. / It's her. The old one, with the faded frill.

A2-03.en: When their frills flush red, something's bothering them. / Red frill, I back off. / Pale frill, I get one step.

A2-05.en: Rule two: foot scraping means leave. / So I turn sideways, eyes down, and I look boring. / Very boring.

A2-06.en: The little one keeps rolling in that grey mud. / Keeps the bugs off, and he smells like the river. / Smart kid.

A2-07.en: Copying the kid. / Wet mud on the arms, on the neck, palm fan over my head. / Now I smell like him.

A2-08.en: Don't move. Don't move. He's coming over by himself. / Mum is watching me very hard right now. / Hi, buddy.

A2-14.en: It walked right past me. / They froze before I heard a single thing. / Their silence is my alarm now.

A2-R3.en: Rule three: standing on the edge makes you bait. / They didn't close the circle for me, / but they let me in.

A2-15.en: Twenty steps away. Big guy looked right at me, kept eating. / I'm not family yet. / But I'm furniture now.

A2-16.en: Problem. This is all the water I've got left. / It's noon, I've walked all morning, / and the creek is full of crocodiles.

A3-01.en: Wait, they're leaving, all of them, same direction. / They know exactly where the water is. / I'm coming with you!

A3-03.en: They walk faster than I run. / Every minute they gain another hundred metres on me. / Keep moving, Nora.

A3-07.en: No, no, no. That was all of it. / The sand just drank my water in two seconds. / And they're gone.

A3-09.en: Fresh tracks, mud's still wet inside. / Heading north, toward those tall swamp trees. / Swamp trees mean water. Follow the feet.

A3-D1.en: Another herd, duck-billed Edmontosaurus. / Trying to read their frills, but they don't have frills. / Zero facial signals.

A3-D3.en: Rule four: frills only work on horned faces. / No faces? Then you listen to the ground. / The earth told them first.

A3-11.en: That's a flying reptile, walking, about my height. / It's hunting small things in the mud. / I'm a small thing.

A3-13.en: Found them, just by reading their feet! / The whole herd, in the only water around. / Slowly now. Low and boring.

A3-W3.en: Rule five: take shifts. They never all drink together. / One head always up, watching the deep. / I drink when she watches.

A3-14.en: Big guy's blocking the water. Frill's red. / Sideways, eyes down, boring. Very boring. / Pale frill. Okay. One step.

A3-15.en: Muddy, cold, and tastes like a dinosaur's foot. / Honestly, best drink of my whole life. / Don't tell anyone.

A3-16.en: Hey, buddy, you found me again. / Arm's length. Closest anyone's let me get all day. / I'll take it.

A3-Q1.en: One hour left. / He's sleeping like it's just another afternoon. / His pulse is beating right through my boot.

A3-17.en: Water. Shade. A herd that tolerates me. / First time today I actually feel safe. Like a holiday. / I almost forgot what today is. Almost.

A4-02.en: Six o'clock. Sun's still up, birds are singing, / nothing looks any different. / Maybe I got the day wrong.

A4-04.en: I knew the hour, the place, the distance. / I thought knowing meant I'd be watching. / I'm not watching.

A4-08.en: Ground wave. The whole valley just rolled like water. / The herd's breaking, they're running. / Get up, get up!

A4-P2.en: Even the king is leaving in a hurry. / Nobody owns this valley anymore.

A4-12.en: It's raining glass, tiny beads, everywhere. / I lost them, I can't see the herd. / Where do I go?

A4-14.en: Herd's going north, into the trees. / The little one's going down, toward the crocodiles. / He hasn't been wrong yet. Follow the kid.

A4-16.en: That hollow under the bank. / The one I skipped this morning because of the crocodiles. / He's already in. Go, go.

MASTER.en: Down, down, the air is burning hot! / Wet mud on the arms, on everything, stay flat. / Pull the frond, boot's still out! / Don't move.

A5-02.en: The glass stopped falling a while ago. / The sky went orange, then brown, then grey. / We're still alive.

A5-06.en: This morning I crawled out of that creek. / Twelve hours later, the whole world just went quiet. / Listen.

A5-07.en: I came here to watch the end. / Turns out the end doesn't need an audience. / Rule six. Follow the kid.
